meta.description: A single tappable segment inside a Segmented Control. 6 variants across State (Default / Pressed / Disabled) × Active (true / false). Active segments fill brand-blue; inactive segments carry a brand-blue outline. (Assessed in the 2026 Working File.)

verdict.title: Keep — a complete state matrix
verdict.text: All four DS Health traits pass and nothing is open. Six variants cover State × isActive, including pressed-active, with token-bound fills and a token-bound outline on inactive segments.

traits.name: Reusable
traits.note: The one segment primitive for every Segmented Control — the row composes N instances at any count, so a single atom covers 2-, 3-, and 4-segment controls.

traits.name: Self-contained
traits.note: Owns its own fill, outline, label, and radius tokens across all six State × Active combinations. No external instance dependencies.

traits.name: Consistent
traits.note: Complete 3 × 2 matrix — State (Default / Pressed / Disabled) × Active (true/false), lowercase booleans. Active segments fill brand-blue, inactive carry the brand-blue outline; pressed and disabled shift the shade predictably.

traits.name: Composable
traits.note: Nests inside the Segmented Control row as an instance, so atom changes propagate to every segment across every item count.

behavior.notes: Fills brand-blue #005CE5 with a white label. The currently-selected segment.
White fill with a 1.5px brand-blue outline and a brand-blue label.
Touch-down feedback — active darkens to #2340A9; inactive shows a light #F6F9FD (72%) fill under the outline.
Muted #9BC5FD for both active fill and inactive outline; tap blocked.

propertyMapping.description: The segment is composed by the parent Segmented Control; neither property is set directly. isActive forwards from the row’s selected index and State derives at runtime, so both are outputs of the row rather than inputs to the segment.

rows.swift: derived — isPressed from the gesture, isEnabled from the environment

rows.figma: label — a TEXT layer, not a confirmed text property

Nothing to set: // the active segment darkens to #2340A9, an inactive one takes // a #F6F9FD 72% wash under its label.

accessibility.ios: Each segment is a .button with .isSelected on the active one.
accessibility.android: Apply Role.RadioButton per segment inside the row’s Modifier.selectableGroup().

accessibility.ios: Announce position in the set — "Label, selected, 1 of 3" — so the user knows how many segments there are.
accessibility.android: Set stateDescription and let selectableGroup() supply the index.

accessibility.ios: The segment is 40.33pt tall — under the 44 × 44pt minimum. Extend with .contentShape rather than resizing; the drawn height belongs to the row.
accessibility.android: Under the 48 × 48dp minimum. Use Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize(), which pads the target without changing the drawn height.

accessibility.ios: Not focusable; .disabled(true) comes from the parent control, so the whole row leaves the focus order together.
accessibility.android: enabled = false on the row; not focusable.

accessibility.requirement: Colour is not the only cue
accessibility.ios: Active versus inactive is carried by fill and label colour alone — no icon, no weight change. Pair the control with a heading that names what is being switched.
accessibility.android: Same. The right-edge divider is decorative and must not be announced.

accessibility.ios: The label is 16pt and must scale; the 40.33pt segment has to grow with it rather than clip.
accessibility.android: Use sp for the label and let the segment height follow fontScale.

usageGuidelines.doText: Let the parent Segmented Control own selection. isActive is index == selectedIndex, and State derives from the gesture and the enabled flag.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t place a segment on its own or drive isActive per instance — two active segments in one row is a state the component cannot express.

usageGuidelines.doText: Treat the right-edge line as a divider between segments. It only renders on inactive segments, which is why it earns its place in a 3- or 4-segment control.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t read it as a border. The stroke is declared on all four sides but only the right one has weight, so an inactive segment is not outlined — it is separated.

usageGuidelines.doText: Keep labels short enough to fit at the row’s widest segment. The segment is 16px padding either side of the label and every segment shares the row’s width equally.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t rely on truncation. The label has no wrap or ellipsis treatment in any of the six variants, so an over-long label pushes the row past its container.

usageGuidelines.doText: Disable the whole row when the choice is unavailable — State=Disabled mutes active and inactive alike, to #9BC5FD.
usageGuidelines.dontText: Don’t disable a single segment to show it is unavailable. There is no per-segment disabled path, and a muted segment beside live ones reads as selected-but-faded.

scorecard.notes: Naming is fine — each variant is a frame with a single label TEXT child, and the old #value node is gone. The defect is the stroke: it is declared on all four sides but only the right one carries weight, so the node reads as a fully outlined button. That is exactly how the previous assessment came to document a "1.5px brand-blue outline" that does not render. Declare the three zero-weight sides off.

State is PascalCase with Title Case values; isActive takes the is prefix with lowercase true/false. The property was Active in the retired 2026 Working File node and now matches the C2 boolean convention.

Fills are internally consistent and reuse the family’s blues, but no segmented-control/* namespace is registered and bindings cannot be read with the Talk To Figma plugin — so the Style tab’s token column is — rather than asserted.
Maps cleanly: isActive forwards from the row’s selected index, State derives from the press gesture and the enabled flag. Nothing here needs a property the platforms do not already have.
Complete 3 × 2 matrix with no gaps — Default, Pressed and Disabled at both isActive values, including the pressed-active frame that the 1.0.0 assessment added.
Text-only segment. No icons, no images, nothing to vectorise.

variants.description: State (3) × isActive (2) = 6. Complete matrix, no gaps. Active segments are a solid fill with a white label; inactive ones have no fill — bar Pressed — and carry a right-edge divider in the state’s own colour.

changelog.header: Repointed to the Sticker Sheets file · node 26628:50752

rows.body: The record assessed a different Figma file. meta.node pointed at 4111:10773 in the 2026 Working File (pbxY8a2xcIfVZKxwnud9Xe); the live component is 26628:50752 in Sticker Sheets v2 (HwWDwPit2xJjDH4zszOZ5o). Every value in this entry is re-read from the latter. Dated when found — nothing records when the move happened.

Inactive segments have a right-edge divider, not an outline. Every tab described "a 1.5px brand-blue outline" around the whole segment. export_node_as_image shows a single vertical line on the right edge only — the stroke is declared on all four sides and just the right one has weight. The component is a segment divider, not a bordered button.
Active renamed isActive. The property now takes the is prefix with lowercase true/false, matching the C2 boolean convention and its siblings in the Radio family.

Two label colours were undocumented. The Colors section listed active and inactive-default labels only. Pressed-inactive is #2340A9 and disabled-inactive is #9BC5FD — both now recorded, so all six variants have a label value.
The pressed-inactive wash carries 72% opacity. Documented as a flat #F6F9FD; the fill is #F6F9FD at 0.72.
Typography resolved to a style name. Primary/Label/Base, matched. Replaces the font spec Proxima Soft Bold · 16 / 16 · +0.25, which the guide bans as a stand-in for a style name.

The Style tab became interactive. The component had no demo script at all — demoControls: [] and a hand-written inline-styled span for a preview. It now has public/scripts/demos/segmented-control-button.js with State and isActive controls, and the preview and the server-rendered markup come from one renderer.
Variants Inventory repointed. Six rows on 4111:* / 4715:* nodes from the retired file, replaced with 26628:50753–26628:50763, each carrying its verified background, divider and label.
Code tab filled in. Installation had no blocks, and Usage Snippets and Usage Guidelines were both empty. Property Mapping used Prop=Value form and is now one prose row per property.
Scorecard note corrected. C1 described layers as container / label; each variant has a single label TEXT child and no container frame. C2 said Active was "retained by design" — it was renamed.

The stroke is declared on four sides with weight on one. That is what made the outline reading look right for two versions. Until the three zero-weight sides are turned off, anyone reading the node sees a fully bordered button.

Divider weight is unread. The Talk To Figma plugin does not return strokeWeight, and the outside-aligned stroke falls outside the SVG export bounds, so get_svg drops it entirely. The preview draws 1px — the one value in the Style tab that is not attested.

The segment is under the minimum touch target. 40.33pt tall against 44 × 44pt on iOS and 48 × 48dp on Android. The Accessibility table says to extend the hit area rather than resize, since the drawn height belongs to the row.

Whether label is an exposed text property is unverified. The layer is named label, not #label, and the property panel was not supplied. If it is not exposed, segment text cannot be set in Figma at all — a gap rather than a documentation issue.
Token bindings unread, so all twelve colour rows carry —. No segmented-control/* namespace is registered; the previous record’s paths were not carried forward because they named the retired file.

The Overview tab still describes the retired node. meta.node, meta.figmaUrl, the description, the verdict and the Behavior table all name 4111:10773, Active, and the 1.5px outline. Overview scope — needs a Component Review run before the page stops contradicting itself.
Component assessed — the single-segment atom for the Segmented Control family. 6 variants across State × Active. Documented
